The number of factors of \( n \) is given by \( (e_1 + 1)(e_2 + 1) \cdots (e_m + 1) \).

To have exactly eight factors, we need to factorize 8 as a product of integers greater than 1. The only way to do this is to have \( n \) in the form of a prime number raised to the power of 7. The smallest prime number is 2.

Thus, the smallest positive integer that has exactly eight distinct positive factors is \( 2^7 = 128 \).

Therefore, the smallest positive integer that has exactly eight distinct positive factors is \(\boxed{128}\).
